root_cause: Production recovery had already moved its canonical state readback to the EU Supavisor pooler, while repository main still lacked the source-controlled recovery runner and the GitHub workflow still encoded the older recovery topology. That runtime/source drift meant a normal redeploy could reintroduce the same PostgREST-dependent failure path.
prevention_rule: The social-publication recovery control plane must use the source-controlled social-recovery-runner with direct EU Supavisor state readback, bounded preparation, bounded per-channel publish_only delegation to the canonical publisher, and fail-closed final readback. Provider runtime parity is owned separately by the publication-delivery recovery lane.

database: Direct production SQL succeeded and reported pg_is_in_recovery=false.
The Supabase project remained ACTIVE_HEALTHY in eu-central-1.
failure_domain: PostgREST/Data API requests had returned HTTP 522 during the incident.
The log query backend also returned a backend error while direct SQL remained healthy.
runtime: social-recovery-runner production uses the EU Supavisor transaction pooler.
The deployed runner v6 skips heavyweight preparation for content_ready claims and otherwise bounds preparation to 60 seconds.
The deployed runner delegates only bounded per-channel publish_only work to powerhouse-social-publisher.
source_repair: social-publication-recovery.yml delegates to social-recovery-runner and contains no /rest/v1 dependency.
supabase/functions/social-recovery-runner/index.ts is reconciled exactly to deployed runner v6.
tests/brain-central-social-publication-authority-v1.test.mjs fails closed if recovery regresses to direct provider primitives or PostgREST.
